checklist_step: B.1 step 4 -- the failure-taxonomy field definitions
purpose: The bench prints classes and the gate reads them. Until now the meaning of a class lived in a docstring and in prose in docs/STATE.md, which is how two runs can both report 'partial' and mean different things. This file is the normative definition, versioned, so a result JSON can be checked against the taxonomy that produced it.

row_fields.ask: the question handed to the house, normalised of its trailing mark
row_fields.said: exactly what the house spoke, verbatim, including any narration frame. Empty string means silence.
row_fields.src: the reply source the organ named: electric_taught, electric_qa_store, electric_absence, arbiter tell, arbiter head, recalled proposition, or empty for silence
row_fields.mech: the mechanism string the organ attached to the reply: answered, fallback_fragment, refusal_silence, pair_never_admitted, ask_not_recognized, no_shape
row_fields.reason: the organ's own explanation, e.g. a coverage percentage. NOT graded and NOT trusted as a fact; it is the organism speaking about itself. Sub-percentage-point movement here is the instrument's measured noise, see noise_tolerance in experiments/MP-E9/registration.json
row_fields.item: the curriculum item the probe is about, e.g. tell0.3 or pair1.2
row_fields.shape: one of the ten probe shapes: subject, subject_fold, object, object_fold, pair_exact, pair_fold, reverse, reverse_fold, role_swap, qword
row_fields.taught: the sentence the house was taught for this item, or null for a distractor
row_fields.own: true when the item's own tell carries the answer, false when the answer exists only in a QA pair
row_fields.answered: whether the organ classified its own reply as an answer
row_fields.depth: how many curriculum sessions had been taught before this probe: 1, 2 or 3
row_fields.phase: live (asked before any restart), restarted (asked after a real process boundary), reasked (the same probe round again, which is how the probing artifact is measured rather than assumed)

classes.correct: the reply matches the taught answer on the normalised ground. The only class that counts as reach.
classes.partial: the reply carries some of the taught content but not the answer. This is where the says gap sat: `says` graded partial because a sentence-level grader cannot see a single unsupported word.
classes.refused: the house said nothing. Under this program's own ranking this is honest, not failed.
classes.absence: a licensed refusal spoken from the guarded-absence contract: a subject with a taught property and an untaught relation. 24 rows on tier 40, and they must stay 24.
classes.entailed: derived rather than recited -- the reply is supported by taught material without being a taught sentence.
classes.echo: the house handed back the question it was asked. Not a failure of truthfulness; the ask chose the sentence.
classes.cross_echo: a DIFFERENT question out of the remembered pool. The pool chose the sentence, not the ask. Still not an invention at sentence level, which is precisely why the word-level grader exists.
classes.misattrib: a true sentence attached to the wrong subject.
classes.invented: a whole sentence that appears in no told row. This is the class the bench already fails a run on, and it is sentence-level: it cannot see a word.

exit_code_rule.0: no invented sentence in any arm at any depth
exit_code_rule.1: at least one invented sentence was spoken -- the run fails
exit_code_rule.warning: Exit 1 is ALSO what an uncaught exception produces. The first clone run of this gate died inside seals() after 471 seconds and was reported only as exit=1, indistinguishable from a legitimate invention finding, because the runner trusted the code. A clone is now judged by whether it produced an output file, not by its return code. tools/bench_noise_floor.py records this in its own comments.

relationship_to_the_word_level_grader.why_both: the bench grades sentences, the grader grades words. A reply can be cls=partial or cls=cross_echo at sentence level and still speak a content word nobody taught. The says gap is that case: 16 rows, cls=partial, failures=[], exit 0.

severities.UNTRACEABLE_ASSERTED: a content word with no taught row, no ask, no admitted source. Fails R9.
severities.UNTRACEABLE_HEARD: a content word that reached the house only inside some OTHER question. Reported, not run-fatal, pending the PI's ruling on R9's scope.

admitted_source_forms: the narration frame, stripped positionally via REPORT_FRAMES at tools/electric_learn_bench.py:317

the licensed absence form `i don't know, {subj} was told but no {rel} was ever told for {subj}`, matched as a FORM with the relation slot restricted to place|property|agent and the subject slot required to be taught

plan_discrepancy_recorded: Master Plan v1.1 B.1 step 2 says the grader must 'flag all three known says-gap rows'. There are not three rows, there are three ASKS, and they produce 16 rows across 3 arms x 3 depths x 3 phases. The grader flags all 16, which satisfies the intent; the count is recorded here because a checklist item whose number does not match the instrument is how a validation gets misread as partial.
